title: 2026 Season Power Rankings
subtitle: Pre-Week 10 board. The Eddies made it seven straight and sit alone in first at 7-2, Hyper dropped 296.5 for the kitty, LAB's 62-point quarterback still couldn't keep them on the bus, and Substation's 280.5 ended the Goats' Last Ride for good, leaving five riders. Tuesday's trades sent George Pickens to Ultron for Kyle Hamilton, moved C.J. Stroud from LAB to Saltese, and swapped Roquan Smith to the SPD's, and Wednesday's waivers saw the Goats spend $42 on Tank Dell and Corey Kiner.
method: W/L + win quality + roster ceiling + FAAB + pedigree + sit/start + trades; PF is evidence, not the ranking.

rankings.blurb: Juice: seven straight after an 0-2 start, and this time they didn't need a tiebreak. The Eddies beat TTAB 276–239.5, the third-best score of the week, and sit alone in first at 7-2 with 2294 PF, third in the WU and still on the bus, $25 left. Tuesday they sent George Pickens to Ultron for Kyle Hamilton. Junk: Hamilton is still stashed on IR, so that trade is a teaser until he's back. LAB visits, fresh off the bus, after trading C.J. Stroud a day after he scored 62.

Juice: 296.5! The Hypersecretors took the week's high and the kitty, beat the SPD's by 44.5, and jumped to second in the WU in PF at 2325. Kenneth Walker III's 44 was the third-best offensive score of the week, and Hyper is 5-4 and still on the bus. Wednesday they moved on from Justin Herbert, spent $2 on Bryce Young, added De'Zhaun Stribling, and cut DeForest Buckner, leaving $10. Junk: that's a thin wallet heading into a trip to Ultron, which just took down the WU's points leader and now has George Pickens.

Juice: still the WU's scoring machine at 2446 PF, 121 clear of Hyper, still on the bus, and $69 is the second-fattest wallet after $8 claims on Troy Dye and Tony Adams. Junk: that scoring crown didn't travel. Pocket has lost three straight — Hyper in Week 7, the SPD's 317.5 in Week 8, and 237–261.5 at Ultron in Week 9 — and 237 was only ninth this week. TTAB visits.

Juice: 271.5, the fourth-best score of the week, and an 83-point beatdown of Saltese (188.5). The Slumlords are 5-4 and climbing. Junk: still $0 in the wallet, and 2208.5 PF ranks only sixth. The 6-3 Goats visit, still second in the standings but coming off the second-lowest score of the week and a Last Ride funeral.

Juice: 280.5, the second-best score of the week, a 66-point win over LAB, and a Last Ride win over the Goats' 195.5, so Substation rides on. Wednesday they added Jakobi Meyers and DeShon Elliott on $0 claims. Junk: winning Last Ride is not the same as getting back on the bus — five teams remain, and Substation isn't one of them. Only $5 left, and 2069.5 PF ranks 11th. The Dongers visit with a three-game winning streak, which is a sentence this board is getting used to.

Juice: still 6-3, still second in the standings, still the stingiest PA in the WU at 1950.5, and Arvell Reese's 62 was the top IDP score of the week. Wednesday they spent $42 — Tank Dell $26, Corey Kiner $16 — and cut Keisean Nixon, leaving $18. Junk: Reese's 62 and they still scored only 195.5, the second-lowest of the week, lost 236–195.5 to Doubtpfizer, and that same 195.5 lost Last Ride to Substation's 280.5, so the Goats are out for good. A trip to the Slumlords is next.

Juice: beat the 6-3 Goats 236–195.5, still on the bus, fourth in the WU in PF at 2246, and $70 is now the fattest wallet in the league after $2 on Hunter Wohler. Junk: still 4-5, and the 2411.5 PA is the worst in the WU. Saltese visits with the week's floor and a brand-new quarterback.

Juice: still on the bus at 4-5, fifth in PF at 2231, and Jordan Love's 47 was the second-best offensive score of the week. Tuesday they added Roquan Smith from LAB for Nathan Landman, with $44 left. Junk: a 47-point quarterback and they still lost 252–296.5 to the kitty winners. That's a 44.5-point hole Love couldn't fill. Morningside visits, last in the WU in PF.

Juice: beat the PF leader 261.5–237 and moved to 4-5. Tuesday they flipped Kyle Hamilton to the Eddies for George Pickens, then Wednesday spent the last $7 — DeMarcco Hellams $6, Barion Brown $1 — and added CJ Daniels for $0. Junk: the wallet is now empty, 2014 PF ranks 13th, and Hyper visits coming off 296.5. That's a tough way to open the new-look receiving room.

Juice: C.J. Stroud's 62 was the top offensive score in the WU, and they're still 5-4 with $50 after $6 on Marcus Jones. Junk: 214.5 was the lowest among the six alive, so they're off the bus after a 66-point loss to Substation, and that's three straight losses. Then on Tuesday they sent the 62-point quarterback to Saltese for Matthew Stafford and Demetrius Knight, and Roquan Smith to the SPD's for Nathan Landman. A trip to the 7-2 Eddies is next.

Juice: 239.5 at the Eddies wasn't a collapse, and $10 is left. Junk: 4-5 after a 276–239.5 loss, 2048.5 PF ranks 12th, and the re-entry dream has been over since Last Ride slipped away in Week 8. A trip to Pocket, the WU's points leader, is next.

Juice: THE DONGERS HAVE A THREE-GAME WINNING STREAK. They beat Morningside 253.5–231.5, David Bailey's 48 was the third-best IDP score of the week, and 2090.5 PF now ranks eighth, ahead of the 6-3 Goats. Jaxon Smith-Njigba's 275 still leads every player in the WU on the year. Junk: still 3-6 with $1 to spend. A trip to Substation, which just dropped 280.5, awaits.

Juice: Carson Schwesinger's 60 was the second-best IDP score of the week, and Tuesday they landed C.J. Stroud — a day after his 62 in a LAB uniform — for Matthew Stafford and Demetrius Knight. Wednesday added Aaron Rodgers, Darnell Washington and Jaquan Brisker on $0 claims. Junk: 188.5 was the lowest score of the week, even with a 60-point linebacker, and they're 3-6 with $3 left. A trip to Doubtpfizer is next.

Juice: 231.5 wasn't the week's floor, and $8 remains. Junk: lost 253.5–231.5 to a Dongers team that's now won three straight, fell to 3-6, and sit dead last in PF at 1856, 158 behind 13th. A trip to the SPD's, who are still on the bus, is next.
